title: KoreLumina — Master OS - Runtime Header Refinement

messages.content:
It depends on which ChatGPT interface you're using, because GitHub integration is still being rolled out and the UI differs.
If you see your GitHub connector in ChatGPT


Click New Chat.


Look for Sources, Connectors, or a + / paperclip button near the message box.


Choose GitHub.


Select your repository (for example, kore20lllc-netizen/korelumina).


Start the conversation.


If the repository is attached correctly, you can ask:

"Find appearance.ts."

or

"Search for executiveMaterial."

without pasting any code.

If you don't see a GitHub option
Your GitHub account may be connected for authentication, but repository browsing may not yet be available in your ChatGPT client or plan.

Let's verify what you have
Tell me:


Are you using ChatGPT on the web (chatgpt.com) or the macOS desktop app?


When you click New Chat, do you see any of these:


GitHub


Connectors


Sources


Add source


A paperclip or + menu with GitHub listed?




Based on your answer, I can tell you exactly where to click.

On the macOS ChatGPT app, the GitHub connector is available only if your account has the repository connector feature enabled. If it is, here's how to access it:


Open New Chat.


Click the + (or paperclip) next to the message box.


Look for Connectors or Add source.


Choose GitHub.


Select your repository (for example, kore20lllc-netizen/korelumina).


Ask your question.


If GitHub is attached, I should be able to answer questions like:


"Find appearance.ts."


"Where is executiveMaterial defined?"


"Trace every use of ProductionNavigator."


without asking you to run terminal commands.
If you don't see GitHub
There are two common reasons:


The GitHub connector hasn't been enabled for your account yet.


The macOS app hasn't exposed the repository picker, even though your GitHub account is connected.


Let's determine which case you're in
When you click the + (or paperclip) beside the prompt, what options do you see? List them exactly, or send a screenshot of that menu. That will tell us whether the repository connector is available or if your GitHub connection is only for account integration rather than repository access.
But how come do I have a GitHub, I can open GitHub on my app on the phone, but not on a Mac operating system?

From your screenshot, this isn't a GitHub permissions issue—it's a feature availability issue.
The menu you opened in the macOS app only shows:


Upload file


Upload photo


Take screenshot


Take photo


There is no "GitHub," "Connectors," or "Add source" entry. That means the desktop app you're using doesn't currently expose the repository connector, even though your GitHub account may be connected elsewhere.
This can happen because:


The iOS app and the macOS app don't always receive new features at the same time.


Connector features are rolled out server-side and can differ by platform.


Having GitHub connected to your ChatGPT account doesn't automatically mean every client can browse repositories.


If GitHub works on your iPhone, it's likely that the iOS app has the repository connector enabled for your account while the macOS app does not.
A few things you can check:


Make sure the macOS app is fully up to date.


Open chatgpt.com in a browser and see if GitHub/Connectors appears there.


If it appears on the web but not in the Mac app, it's a client limitation rather than an account issue.


Once the macOS app gains the same connector support, our KoreLumina workflow would become much simpler. I could inspect the repository directly, trace symbols, read files, and propose minimal terminal patches without repeatedly asking you to run grep, sed, or cat commands.
